title: White Rice with Lentils and Added Fat

content.title: About
content.content: White rice with lentils and added fat is a ready‑to‑eat product that combines boiled white rice, cooked lentils, and vegetable fats. It provides the carbohydrates of rice, plant protein from lentils, and the energy density of fats, making it a convenient meal for quick nutrition.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The rice‑lentil combination is traditional in Middle Eastern and Mediterranean cuisines.
Lentils are one of the oldest cultivated legumes, grown for over 8,000 years.
Added vegetable fats improve absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins such as vitamin E.
The dish is often used in sports nutrition because of its high calorie and protein content.
The white rice is polished, reducing fiber but making it softer and faster to digest.

items.title: Energy supply
items.content: The mix of carbohydrates and fats provides a quick and sustained energy boost, useful during intense physical activity.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: Lentils supply plant‑based protein that supports muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Source of iron and folate
items.content: Lentils are a good source of iron and folic acid, essential for blood formation and metabolism.

items.title: Supports cardiovascular health
items.content: Vegetable fats, especially monounsaturated fatty acids, may help lower LDL cholesterol.

items.title: Easy to digest
items.content: Boiled rice and soft lentils are gentle on the stomach, suitable for people with sensitive digestion.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: Added fats increase the calorie count, so portion control is important for weight‑managed diets.

items.title: Possible gluten cross‑contamination
items.content: While rice and lentils are naturally gluten‑free, processing equipment may be shared with gluten‑containing foods.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to lentils.

items.title: Sodium level
items.content: If the product is seasoned, monitor sodium intake, especially for people with hypertension.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The product is ready to eat straight from the package. It can be served as a standalone meal, added to salads, used as a side dish for meat or fish, or reheated in a microwave or on the stovetop.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place with the package tightly sealed. For long‑term storage (over 6 months) keep refrigerated to prevent fat oxidation.
